subject: Secure inference: constraints and next steps
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Secure inference: constraints and next steps

Hi Elaine —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and the next steps we discussed so there’s a single source of truth. Please correct me where I’m off.

Key pain points you raised:
- Data residency: all patient data must remain within US regions; any backups also must not leave region.
- Regulatory/air-gap driver: internal security expects an "isolated ingestion" option (no outbound internet from inference hosts) for pilot customers in the first 12 months.
- Network constraints: strict egress rules, proxy/forwarding required for telemetry, and only a handful of whitelisted IPs allowed from vendor endpoints.
- Procurement timeline: procurement wants pricing and residency options before 2026-12-15 to slot into their Q4 budget cycle.

Goals we captured:
- Production target: ~100 RPS inference for 512-token average requests, p95 latency target <150ms for most routes.
- SLA: enterprise SLA with scheduled maintenance windows and audit logs retained 12+ months.
- Cost envelope: team is targeting a commitment that keeps unit cost predictable for the pilot phase.

Immediate next steps (owners):
1) Redwood to produce a short technical acceptance checklist and an architecture sketch showing an air-gapped / VPC-hosted option. (Owner: Ben — due 2026-12-01)
2) Redwood to compile SOC2/Security evidence summary and sample data flow description for internal review. (Owner: Karthik — due 2026-12-02)
3) NovoMed to introduce procurement contact and any additional security approvers. (Owner: Elaine)

Attachments: I’ve attached a short text recap and will add the architecture sketch after Ben shares it.

Proposed meeting: if helpful, we can do a 30-minute tech deep dive with your infra/security team the week of 2026-12-06.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the checklist and sketch when available.

—
Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@novomed.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Secure inference: constraints and next steps

Sofia — thanks for the clear recap. That aligns with our notes. A couple of clarifications and context from my side:

- Procurement: looping in procurement@novomed.com for pricing and contract cadence. They need a pricing sheet and residency options by 2026-12-15.
- KMS/HSM: we require HSM-backed key storage (cloud KMS integration acceptable but must meet FedRAMP Moderate-equivalent controls).
- Telemetry: security has asked that telemetry either be pushed over an allowlisted proxy or batched to a collector in our VPC; no direct vendor connections to external analytics endpoints.
- Whitelist: we’ll provide a CIDR/IP whitelist; please confirm if Redwood can support a small set of egress IPs per deployment.

I attached a short L3 doc that lists our current network constraints and the org contact for security review (see attachment).

I’ll also introduce Rajesh from procurement in a separate message so he can track commercial terms.

Thanks — Elaine

Summary asks from NovoMed:
- Air-gapped / isolated hosting option for pilot (no outbound internet from inference hosts).
- Ability to limit telemetry (option to route via their proxy + whitelist egress IPs).
- HSM/KMS integration and evidence for key management controls.
- Residency enforcement and proof points (audit log retention, backups within region).

Ben — can you draft a 1-page acceptance checklist + basic architecture sketch showing an isolated VPC deployment and any optional outbound relays? If an air-gapped variant requires additional infra (e.g., relay hosts, local ingress workers), call that out and a rough capacity/cost delta.

Karthik — can you pull our SOC2 evidence summary and a short notes doc on key management integration options we can share with their security team?

I’ve added the HubSpot record below for reference and will share the drive folder once Ben uploads the sketch.

Sofia — noted. Quick operational read: we can support an isolated VPC deployment with restricted egress. High-level notes:

- Architecture sketch: will upload an initial PNG (architecture-sketch-v1.png) to the shared drive by EOD 2026-12-01. It will show local ingress workers, an internal inference pool, and an optional egress relay in the customer VPC for batched telemetry.
- IP whitelisting: we can support a small set of static egress IPs per deployment; if they want totally zero egress we’ll need a relay pattern that runs entirely inside the customer VPC (adds ~1-2 infra nodes and increases pilot cost estimate by ~12-18%).
- KMS/HSM: we support cloud KMS integrations; for stricter HSM requirements we’ll document the integration approach and any limitations (we may need SOC/attestation coordination with their cloud provider).
- Evidence pack: Karthik — if you can prep the SOC2 summary and KMS note, I’ll add the operational checklist items and a short cost delta table.

I’ll flag any follow-up questions after I post the sketch.

— Ben
